How Does Transfer Certificate (TC) Management Work?

Long image

A

Answer

Official Transfer Certificates (TC) and Conduct Certificates are generated only after 100% of college department clearances are approved, verified, and locked by the Clerk Desk.

  1. Students initiate a digital No-Dues clearance request across assigned campus departments and laboratories.
  2. Automated system gatekeepers strictly block certificate generation if any department due is unpaid or pending.
  3. Clerks review student particulars, fee clearance, and promotion status before setting an immutable lock.
  4. Generation produces audit-tracked versions with deterministic certificate numbering and digital QR stamps.

What is the step-by-step path from student request to certificate printing?

Diagram structure
  • Clerk Imports Roster roster
  • Student Submits Request req
  • Departments Clear Dues depts
  • 100% Clearance Gate? gate
  • Clerk Reviews Dossier review
  • Final-Verify and Lock lock
  • Generate Version v1 gen
  • Dual Print and QR print
  • depts → gate · All Approved
  • gate → review · 100% Clear
  • gen → print · Ready to Print
  • lock → gen · is_locked = 1
  • req → depts · Dispatch
  • review → lock · Data Confirmed
  • roster → req · PIN & Master
  1. Clerk Imports Roster ↗

    The administrative clerk bulk-imports student roster with PIN, admission number, and branch.

  2. Student Submits Request ↗

    The student logs in and dispatches digital No-Dues requests to all assigned campus departments.

  3. Departments Clear Dues ↗

    Library, Sports, Hostel, Exam Cell, and Labs inspect accounts and record clearances.

  4. 100% Clearance Gate ↗

    The system validates every clearance node; pending dues strictly block certificate issuance.

  5. Clerk Reviews Dossier ↗

    The clerk opens the TC console to confirm leaving date, conduct, and promotion status.

  6. Final-Verify and Lock ↗

    The clerk locks the record, setting is_locked = 1 with clerk username and timestamp.

  7. Generate Version v1 ↗

    The system computes deterministic T. No and saves an immutable v1 certificate record.

  8. Dual Print and QR ↗

    Both student and clerk can print the official Transfer and Conduct Certificates.

How does the system prevent unauthorized or premature certificate issuance?

Security SafeguardTraditional Paper ProcessSVGP Digital TC System
Pending Dues CheckVulnerablePhysical signatures can be skipped or forgedStrict GateAutomated query requires 100% clearance
Record TamperingUnverifiedHandwritten certificates altered after signingTamper-ProofDossier locked (is_locked = 1) before creation
Data AmendmentsNo TraceDamaged or lost paper duplicates without historyAudit TrailVersioning archives older issues (v1, v2)
Number AssignmentCollisionsManual book registers prone to duplicate numbersCollision-FreeDeterministic T. No derived directly from PIN
Role BoundariesUnrestrictedAny office staff can access blank printed stationaryEnforced RBACRBAC restricts locking and generation to Clerk role

What is the API interaction sequence during verification and locking?

Diagram structure
  • Clerk Desk clerk
  • Clerk Controller api
  • PostgreSQL Database db
  • clerk → api · POST /api/clerk/certificates/lock {student_pin}
  • api → db · SELECT FROM no_dues_requests WHERE status='Completed'
  • db → api · 100% Clearance Confirmed
  • api → db · UPDATE certificate_data SET is_locked = 1
  • db → api · Lock Acknowledged
  • api → clerk · 200 OK (Certificate Data Locked)
  • clerk → api · POST /api/clerk/certificates/generate {student_pin}
  • api → db · INSERT INTO certificate_versions (v1, t_no, timestamp)
  • db → api · Version v1 Created
  • api → clerk · 201 Created (Certificate v1 Ready)
